# Shepherd of Hermas Chapter 26 — The EMET Bible (Literal)

**Translator:** EMET | **Source:** Codex Sinaiticus (ch 1-31) / P.Mich. 130 (ch 32+), Shepherd of Hermas 26 | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-EC/SHE_026_page_001.jpg

---

## Mandate 1 — Believe in One God

**1** First of all, believe that God is one, who created and completed all things and made all things out of nothing to exist, who contains all things, and is himself alone uncontained. **2** Believe in him therefore and fear him; fearing him, exercise self-control. Keep these things and you will throw off all wickedness from yourself and clothe yourself with every virtue of righteousness, and you will live to God if you keep this commandment.

---

*EMET note: Mandate 1 is the shortest of the twelve mandates — a single compact theological statement. Its monotheism is explicit: God is one, creator ex nihilo, unlimited, uncontained. The ethical imperatives follow directly from theological conviction: believing → fearing → self-control → virtue → life with God.*
